title: A colour walk: find something red, yellow, blue and green
description: Take a walk and hunt with your eyes: something red, something yellow, something blue, something green. A simple game that makes a familiar street look brand new.

body.heading: How to play
paragraphs: Before you set off, say the colours out loud together: red, yellow, blue and green. Then walk slowly, and whenever you spot one of the colours, point and shout it out: “Red! A post box!” “Yellow! A flower!”
You do not pick anything up — your eyes do all the collecting. When you have found all four colours, start again and try to find each colour in a smaller thing than last time.

body.heading: Harder hunts for champion spotters
paragraphs: Found everything too fast? Add purple and orange. Still too easy? Hunt for two colours on the same thing — a stripy shirt, a painted door, a bird with a coloured chest.
On the way home, try to remember one thing for every colour without looking. Your brain will surprise you with how much it kept.

body.heading: Rainy-day version
paragraphs: No walk today? Play the same game in one room of your house, or with a picture book: turn the pages and hunt the colours there.
Colours are hiding everywhere. Once your eyes learn to hunt them, even a grey day has red, yellow, blue and green in it somewhere.

takeaway: Hunt colours with your eyes on a walk — red, yellow, blue, green — and a familiar street becomes a treasure map.
supervision: An adult walks with the child at all times, holds hands near roads, and chooses a safe, familiar route.
safetyNotes: Hold an adult's hand near roads and only cross at safe crossing places.
Look with your eyes only — do not pick flowers or touch animals, and stay on paths.
screenFreeExtension: At home, sort your toys or crayons into colour piles and see which colour you own most of.
